transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Time: 11:00 AM - 11:52 AM UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Ethan Marshall (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Auriga Head of Security), Daniel Ruiz (Auriga Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (Auriga Procurement)
Links shared: https://redwood.example/soc2 (SOC2 link), https://drive.redwood/example/auriga-caik-draft (CAIQ draft), diagram: https://redwood.example/diagrams/kms-options.png

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of vendor questionnaire items (SIG/CAIQ overlap), focus on KMS options, audit logs, data residency constraints for Auriga's EU + APAC customers. Agreed to send SOC 2 Type II and CAIQ draft and to plan a deeper KMS scoping call. Some minor transcript noise, noted places where system auto-labeled speakers incorrectly.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 coverage and evidence packaging
- CAIQ vs customer security form mapping
- Encryption at rest / in transit and KMS (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)
- Audit log retention and log delivery options
- Data residency and region pinning / private deployment options
- Proof artifacts and timeline for procurement

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
00:00:05 Laura Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining um we really appreciate you taking the time today, I'm Laura from Redwood, AE on the account
00:00:12 Maya Patel: Hi Laura, thanks, hi all. quick note, running a bit short on time so we'll try to keep to the agenda, we have 50 minutes total
00:00:20 Ethan Marshall: Morning, Ethan here, I'll focus on the technical pieces — KMS, logs, on-prem options etc.
00:00:30 Priya Singh: Priya from procurement. we'll need the evidence pack for our supplier review by the 23rd, so timeline is tight
00:00:38 Laura Kim: totally noted, Priya. quick walk through plan: we'll map the SIG/CAIQ items you're most concerned about, then Ethan will run through KMS and log mechanics, and we'll close with explicit next steps
00:00:52 Daniel Ruiz: sounds good. for context we run primary workloads in eu-west-1 and a smaller cluster in ap-southeast-2, we have customer data flagged as pii and some regulated data flows to local partners
00:01:10 Maya Patel: yes and Auriga requires encryption keys under our control for specific customers, and we have a question on how Redwood supports that model
00:01:21 Laura Kim: ok, high-level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. for KMS we offer two patterns: Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys, and customer-managed keys (CMK) integrated via customer KMS — Ethan will drill into that
00:01:40 Ethan Marshall: right, so a couple of variants — 1) Redwood-managed: we hold keys in our HSM, rotate per policy, provide attestation; 2) Customer-managed: you provide a KMS grant/role and we use APIs to encrypt/decrypt, we never persist plaintext; 3) Hybrid — for Dedicated we can enable a per-customer host key, still managed by Redwood infra but with stricter separation
00:02:05 Maya Patel: when you say "never persist plaintext" can you clarify? we need specifics for the SIG answer and evidence
00:02:15 Ethan Marshall: yes, good call, sorry shorthand — request flow: user request arrives, tokens go to runtime with ephemeral KV cache, we store only encrypted blobs at rest; plaintext is kept only in memory transiently and never written to disk, the KV cache for longer-context is encrypted with the KMS key before persistence. If audit wants to see the flow we can provide sequence diagrams and runtime logs
00:02:45 Priya Singh: The procurement team will need the attestation doc and how long logs are retained, our legal requires 12 month retention for access logs
00:02:55 Laura Kim: got it. Redwood's default audit logs retention is 90 days in hosted, but for enterprise we can extend to 1 year or export to your SIEM. There are three export options: push to S3 (customer-owned), push syslog to your collector, or streaming to your SIEM via connector
00:03:20 Daniel Ruiz: If we asked for log streaming to our S3 in eu-west-1, is that supported and is encryption applied server-side?
00:03:30 Ethan Marshall: Yes, supported — we can write to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1 using an assumed role and SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS. If you prefer, we can use your CMK for the destination encryption as well. There's a slight latency when delivering logs but it's near real-time for audit events
00:03:55 Maya Patel: For the CAIQ, can you point us to which controls map to customer-managed KMS and which to network isolation? we have a combined questionnaire so need a mapping table
00:04:08 Laura Kim: we maintain a CAIQ mapping doc — we'll share a draft. high-level: KMS questions map to ENCRYPT-* controls, key lifecycle to CRYPTO* items, and network isolation touches on NETWORK-ISOLATION and VPC configurations — we'll include the mapping and call out evidence artifacts like configuration screenshots, KMS policies, and rotation logs
00:04:35 Daniel Ruiz: On private deployment — we may need on-prem for a small set of EU clients. what changes materially for KMS and logs there?
00:04:45 Ethan Marshall: On-prem gives you full control: you host the runtime, keys remain in your KMS/HSM, logs never leave your network unless you push them. The tradeoff is you run the infra; Redwood provides the control plane or a private control plane option depending on the package. There's also the Dedicated option which keeps us in the loop but can be configured for VPC peering and customer-managed keys
00:05:10 Priya Singh: procurement question quickly — do you have SOC2 Type II? we need the report and AICPA statements
00:05:18 Laura Kim: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II for the relevant period. I'll attach the PDF and the cover letter. we'll also include our recent penetration test summary where permitted
00:05:30 Maya Patel: any certifications for ISO? we have an ISO-27001 requirement for some customers
00:05:36 Laura Kim: Redwood is in progress on ISO; we have ISO controls being addressed, ETA for certification is Q4 2026. We'll note that status in the CAIQ where it flags ISO controls
00:05:50 Daniel Ruiz: back to keys — in the customer-managed model, what's the connectivity pattern, does the runtime call the KMS in the customer's VPC or via public API? network egress concerns are real for us
00:06:03 Ethan Marshall: for hosted customers, we call the customer's KMS via public API with hardened TLS and mutual auth where available. For Dedicated or Private, you can enable a private link or peering so KMS traffic stays on the private network. We'll supply network diagrams and the required firewall rules
00:06:25 Maya Patel: transcript hiccup, system mis-labeled a line earlier — but ok. about audit logs, can you provide proof that retention extension is configurable and not just a statement?
00:06:37 Laura Kim: yes, we'll include sample S3 manifests, a retention config screenshot from our console, and an example exporter config. We'll redact any customer-specific PII before sharing
00:06:52 Daniel Ruiz: in the CAIQ answers we'd like to include a note about key rotation frequency, can you confirm default rotation cadence and whether that's overridden in a CMK scenario
00:07:02 Ethan Marshall: default rotation is 90 days for our managed keys; for CMK we defer to your KMS policy, so rotation is controlled by customer policy. We'll document that explicitly in the CAIQ answer
00:07:15 Priya Singh: procurement will also ask for SLAs around data residency breaches or incidents, do you have an incident response time commitment?
00:07:25 Laura Kim: for enterprise contracts we offer an incident response SLA with predefined severity levels; typical initial response within 1 hour for Sev1, full remediation timeline depends on case. We'll include the standard incident response playbook excerpt
00:07:40 Maya Patel: side question: when you say "ephemeral KV cache" earlier — is that encrypted separately or under the same KMS envelope?
00:07:50 Ethan Marshall: KV cache values are encrypted with a runtime envelope key which itself is wrapped by the KMS key. For CMK mode the envelope key is wrapped by your CMK. There's a short-lived lifecycle for the envelope key — rotated frequently and kept in memory. We'll provide a sequence diagram to show this flow
00:08:12 Daniel Ruiz: can you share samples of the audit log schema? we need field-level mappings to our SIEM rules
00:08:20 Ethan Marshall: yes, we'll include the schema (timestamp, user_id, request_id, model_id, action, rt_ms, status, masked_prompt_hash) — note prompts are redacted/masked in logs by default, and full prompt capture is only available in dedicated/private with consent
00:08:40 Maya Patel: masking — can you prove the masking is irreversible? our privacy team will want that
00:08:48 Ethan Marshall: masking is a deterministic hash with peppering per-tenant; we can provide the hashing doc and the code reference in the repo we use for masking. For on-prem you control the peppering secret
00:09:05 Priya Singh: stepping back to the questionnaire — if we provide our internal form, can Redwood map answers and provide an export to upload to our portal?
00:09:16 Laura Kim: yes we can map. add the form to the shared drive and we'll produce a marked-up export. we'll also annotate which items require evidence and what that evidence looks like
00:09:30 Maya Patel: can we get a small demo of how the console shows key usage and logs? that'll help procurement and security to sign off quicker
00:09:40 Ethan Marshall: sure we can do a 20-minute demo — but given time now we'll just highlight screens: key management UI, rotate key button, CMK binding flow, log export settings — we'll schedule a follow-up demo with account admin access
00:09:58 Laura Kim: note — follow-up demo to include live KMS UI, log export, and CAIQ walkthrough. we'll include sample artifacts in advance
00:10:07 Daniel Ruiz: re: data residency — if we pin to eu-west-1 for storage but allow inference routing in us-east for burst, is that acceptable for your architecture or will it expose data to other regions?
00:10:22 Ethan Marshall: that pattern is allowed but you must control which model variants are routed. We can set policy that tokens and persistent storage remain in eu-west-1; ephemeral compute can be routed but we ensure redaction/egress rules and we can limit model variants in other regions. We'll add recommended routing policy config to the docs
00:10:45 Maya Patel: anything about third-party subprocessors? procurement wants the subprocessors list and narrative on control over those subprocessors
00:10:55 Laura Kim: yes, we'll share the current subprocessors list and the subprocessor agreement excerpt. We also have SOC2 coverage for subprocessors and the mapping table to CAIQ controls
00:11:10 Priya Singh: procurement needs pricing bracketing for dedicated vs hosted with CMK add-on, is that something you can send?
00:11:18 Laura Kim: yes we'll include a pricing line item sheet — hosted + CMK add-on vs Dedicated baseline vs Private on-prem one-time fee. pricing will be high-level in the CAIQ bundle and we'll follow up with detailed commercials in a separate email
00:11:35 Maya Patel: ok great. quick clarifying question on evidence: do you provide raw KMS rotation logs or just attestations?
00:11:43 Ethan Marshall: we can provide rotation logs for managed keys (audit trail), and for CMK you'll provide the rotation logs from your KMS. We'll aggregate timeline evidence — e.g., rotation timestamps, operator IDs, and hash digests
00:12:00 Laura Kim: alright, I know we covered a lot — any final quick items?
00:12:05 Daniel Ruiz: just one: is there an offline packaging of evidence you can hand to auditors? sometimes they want a zip of artifacts
00:12:12 Laura Kim: yes, we can build an evidence bundle — sanitized — containing screenshots, config snippets, signed attestations, and the SOC2 PDF. We'll coordinate scope with Maya
00:12:25 Maya Patel: that sounds good. please mark sensitive items to redact and show what will be redacted
00:12:30 Laura Kim: will do. we'll add redaction notes to the bundle manifest
00:12:36 Priya Singh: procurement note — we may need vendor references; can you share two existing customers under NDA that allowed reference checks?
00:12:44 Laura Kim: yes, I'll check with legal and share up to two references that match your vertical.
00:12:53 Ethan Marshall: logging note — for the dedicated option we also support per-tenant log buckets with enforced bucket policies so your security team gets exclusive access
00:13:07 Maya Patel: good. ok let's wrap; next steps cover sending docs and scheduling the deep technical scoping and demo

(crosstalk and small interruptions during scheduling around 00:13:20 - 00:13:50)

00:13:50 Laura Kim: recap and next steps: 1) Redwood sends SOC2, CAIQ draft, KMS diagram and audit log schema by 2026-06-15. 2) Schedule KMS+logs scoping call (Ethan + Daniel) week of 6/22. 3) Auriga to provide data residency constraints and internal questionnaire by 6/18. 4) Redwood to prepare evidence bundle sample and pricing sheet.
00:14:30 Maya Patel: ok thanks all
00:14:33 Priya Singh: thanks, bye
00:14:35 Laura Kim: thanks everyone, bye
